summary: TLS renegotiation spike causing client connection resets and downstream 5xx wave with runtime GPU fragmentation
description: Issue summary: Starting 2026-03-13 22:05 UTC BrightChat reported sustained increase in 5xx responses from the Redwood API for a subset of tenant routes. Error traces show a mix of 502/503 from the API gateway and upstream runtime connection resets and occasional runtime OOM exits. Impact: customer requests failing at ~18-30% error rate for ~30 minutes, affecting chat generation and streaming sessions for BrightChat production traffic.
steps_to_reproduce: 1) Customer workload: sustained long-lived streaming connections with token bursts every ~3s. 2) Simulate TLS renegotiation by triggering LB cert rotation on a small subset of front-end instances. 3) Observe connection resets at the gateway and cascading RTT increases to serving runtime. 4) Observe runtime logs for repeated GPU allocation failures and elevated pagefaults.
logs:
[api-gw] 2026-03-13T22:06:12Z WARN conn reset from 10.12.4.22: TLS renegotiation detected
[lb] 2026-03-13T22:06:10Z INFO starting cert rotation batch id=rot-20260313-2
[runtime] 2026-03-13T22:06:18Z ERROR kvcache alloc failed: cudaMalloc failed (out of memory) size=2.1GB
[runtime] 2026-03-13T22:07:01Z ERROR runtime pid=4421 exit_code=137 signal=OOM_kill
[metrics] 2026-03-13T22:06-22:12 error_rate=0.27 latency_p99=1.4s
investigation_notes: Initial hypothesis: TLS renegotiation caused a wave of connection resets at API gateway leading to request retries and short lived spikes of concurrent connections to certain runtime workers. The runtime workers handling those retries had fragmented GPU memory due to long-lived KV cache entries and incremental prefix caches, which caused cudaMalloc failures and eventual OOM kills when bursty replays increased peak live allocations. Evidence: correlation between LB cert rotation window and error_rate spike; runtime logs showing repeated small allocation failures prior to full OOM; flamegraphs show increased allocator churn on affected workers. Additional finding: gateway configured to retry on 5xx with minimal jitter amplified the storm.
comments: 2026-03-13 22:20 - Support (Aisha): Customer BrightChat reporting 20-30% failures on /v1/chat/stream during rotation window. Asked for request IDs and sample traces.

2026-03-13 22:28 - Oncall SRE (Marco): Confirmed spikes in api-gateway error responses and upstream connection resets. Noted cert rotation started at 22:06 UTC. Paging runtime team for OOM investigation.

2026-03-13 22:42 - Runtime Eng (Dana): Found repeated cudaMalloc errors on 3 of 8 workers; processes hit soft OOM then were killed. Memory fragmentation observed alongside large pinned KV cache entries. Proposing restart of affected workers and temporary eviction of KV cache for BrightChat tenant.

2026-03-13 23:05 - Support (Aisha): Applied mitigation: disabled LB in-place renegotiation for next rotation and increased API gateway connection max and retry backoff for affected deployment. Notified customer of temporary remediation steps.
2026-03-14 02:10 - SRE (Marco): Post-restart metrics show error_rate dropped to baseline <1% and no further runtime OOMs. Filing follow-up for allocator improvements and safer retry policies.
resolution: Mitigation steps executed: 1) Temporarily disabled TLS renegotiation on LB fleet for 2 rotation batches; 2) increased gateway connection limits and introduced exponential jitter on retries for affected routes; 3) restarted 3 impacted runtime pods to compact GPU memory and evicted BrightChat tenant KV cache entries; 4) drained and relaunched workers with a reduced KV cache retention window. Result: error rate returned to baseline within ~40 minutes and streaming stability restored.
postmortem_followups: 1) Add guardrail in LB rotation to avoid in-place renegotiation during high-load windows. 2) Implement runtime allocator compaction pass and limit per-tenant pinned KV cache by memory footprint. 3) Adjust api-gateway retry policy to include exponential backoff + jitter for 5xx upstreams. 4) Add alerting rule correlating LB rotation events with upstream 5xx spikes. Owner: Marco/Runtime Eng. Target dates: fix proposals by 2026-04-01.
